METADATA.title: Do Replaced Pickups Hurt Your Vintage Guitar's Value?
METADATA.description: See how pickup swaps, routing and rewinds affect a vintage guitar. I'll explain missing originals, PAF decals and why removed parts should stay with it.
METADATA.h1: Do Replaced Pickups Hurt A Vintage Guitar's Value?
METADATA.primaryQuery: do replaced pickups devalue a guitar

OUTLINE.text: Pickup Changes And Their Value Effect
Sound And Originality Answer Different Questions
Why Gibson PAFs Need Their Own Assessment

mainEntity.name: Do Replaced Pickups Lower Vintage Guitar Value?

acceptedAnswer.text: A swap without routing can mean about 25 percent less than a comparable original as a broad vintage Les Paul reference. The model, missing pickups and surviving original parts need their own assessment.

mainEntity.name: Does Routing Hurt More Than A Simple Swap?

acceptedAnswer.text: Routing for a different pickup can mean 35 to 40 percent less than a comparable original. The change removes wood, so putting the old pickup back doesn't restore the original body.

A rewind can make an original pickup usable again while retaining some original components. It should be disclosed because the factory winding has changed. The quality and extent of the repair need to be assessed.

mainEntity.name: Do Scratches Under A PAF Decal Prove It Is Fake?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Factory scuffing in the decal area and lengthwise brushing are normal. Fresh, bright abrasion through older patina beneath a new-looking decal is the warning that needs closer inspection.

mainEntity.name: Should I Reinstall The Originals Before Selling?

acceptedAnswer.text: Keep them with the guitar and get an assessment first. Reinstalling parts doesn't erase the work history, and the buyer should be told what was changed and what survives.
